sentences.en: So what I'm going to talk about to you today is something called Ethnography.
sentences.zh: 那么，我今天要向大家介绍的是所谓的人类学研究方法（民族志）。

sentences.en: This is a type of research aimed at exploring the way human cultures work.
sentences.zh: 这是一种旨在探索人类文化运作方式的研究方法。

sentences.en: It was first developed for use in anthropology, and it's also been used in sociology and communication studies.
sentences.zh: 它最初是为人类学而发展起来的，后来也被应用于社会学和传播学研究。

sentences.en: So what's it got to do with business, you may ask.
sentences.zh: 那么，你可能会问：这跟商业有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: Well, businesses are finding that ethnography can offer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，企业发现，民族志研究能够提供。

sentences.en: them deeper insight into the possible needs of customers, either present or future, as well as providing valuable information about their attitudes towards existing products.
sentences.zh: 对企业现有或潜在客户可能需求的更深入洞察，同时还能提供有关客户对现有产品态度的宝贵信息。

sentences.en: And ethnography can also help companies to design new products or services that customers really want.
sentences.zh: 此外，民族志研究还能帮助企业设计出客户真正需要的新产品或服务。

sentences.en: Let's look at some examples of how ethnographic research works in business.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看一些民族志研究在商业中实际应用的例子。

sentences.en: One team of researchers did a project for a company manufacturing kitchen equipment.
sentences.zh: 一个研究团队曾为一家厨房设备制造公司开展了一项研究项目。

sentences.en: They watched how cooks used measuring cups to measure out things like sugar and flour.
sentences.zh: 他们观察厨师如何使用量杯来称量糖、面粉等食材。

sentences.en: They saw that the cooks had to check and recheck the contents, because although the measuring cups had numbers inside them, the cooks couldn't see these easily.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，厨师不得不反复检查量杯内的刻度，因为尽管量杯内壁标有刻度数字，但厨师却难以清晰地看到这些数字。

sentences.en: So a new design of cup was developed to overcome this problem, and it was a top seller.
sentences.zh: 因此，一种新型量杯应运而生，成功解决了这一问题，并成为畅销产品。

sentences.en: Another team of ethnographic researchers looked at how cell phones were used in Uganda, in Africa.
sentences.zh: 另一支民族志研究团队则考察了非洲乌干达地区手机的使用情况。

sentences.en: They found that people who didn't have their own phones could pay to use the phones of local entrepreneurs.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，没有私人手机的人可以付费使用当地企业家提供的手机。

sentences.en: Because these customers paid in advance for their calls, they were eager to know how much time they'd spent on the call so far.
sentences.zh: 由于这些用户需预先支付通话费用，因此他们迫切希望实时了解自己已通话时长。

sentences.en: So the phone company designed phones for use globally with this added feature.
sentences.zh: 于是，该手机公司便设计出一款具备此功能的全球通用手机。

sentences.en: Ethnographic research has also been carried out in computer companies.
sentences.zh: 民族志研究也已在计算机公司中展开。

sentences.en: In one company, IT systems administrators were observed for several weeks.
sentences.zh: 在某家公司中，研究人员连续数周观察了IT系统管理员的工作。

sentences.en: It was found that a large amount of their work involved communicating with colleagues in order to solve problems, but that they didn't have a standard way of exchanging information from spreadsheets and so on.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，他们大量工作内容涉及与同事沟通以解决问题，但却缺乏标准化的方式共享电子表格等信息。

sentences.en: So the team came up with an idea for software that would help them to do this.
sentences.zh: 因此，该研究团队提出了一款软件构想，以协助他们实现这一目标。

sentences.en: In another piece of research, a team observed and talked to nurses working in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 在另一项研究中，一支研究团队观察并访谈了医院工作的护士。

sentences.en: This led to the recognition that the nurses needed to access the computer records of their patients, no matter where they were.
sentences.zh: 这项研究促使人们认识到：无论身处何地，护士都需要随时访问患者的电脑病历。

sentences.en: This led to the development of a portable computer tablet that allowed the nurses to check records in locations throughout the hospital.
sentences.zh: 由此催生了一款便携式电脑平板设备，使护士可在医院各处随时查阅患者记录。

sentences.en: Occasionally, research can be done even in environments where the researchers can't be present.
sentences.zh: 有时，即便研究人员无法亲临现场，相关研究仍可开展。

sentences.en: For example, in one project done for an airline. respondents used their smartphones to record information during airline trips, in a study aiming at tracking the emotions of passengers during a flight.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一项为航空公司开展的研究项目中，受访者在乘机过程中使用智能手机记录相关信息，以追踪乘客在飞行期间的情绪变化。

sentences.en: So what makes studies like these different from ordinary research?
sentences.zh: 那么，这类研究与普通研究有何不同？

sentences.en: Let's look at some of the general principles behind ethnographic research in business.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看商业领域中民族志研究背后的一些基本原则。

sentences.en: First of all, the researcher has to be completely open-minded• he or she hasn't thought up a hypothesis to be tested, as is the case in other types of research.
sentences.zh: 首先，研究人员必须完全秉持开放心态——他/她不会像其他类型研究那样事先提出待验证的假设。

sentences.en: Instead they wait for the participants in the research to inform them.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们等待研究参与者主动提供信息。

sentences.en: As far as choosing the participants themselves is concerned, that's not really all that different from ordinary research - the criteria according to which the participants are chosen may be something as simple as the age bracket they fall into, or the researchers may select.
sentences.zh: 至于参与者自身的遴选方式，其实与普通研究并无太大差异——选择标准可能非常简单，比如仅按年龄分段；研究人员也可能依据收入水平进行筛选；

sentences.en: them according to their income, or they might try to find a set of people who all use a particular a Audioscripts product, for example.
sentences.zh: 或者尝试寻找一组均使用某特定产品的人员，例如。

sentences.en: But it's absolutely crucial to recruit the right people as participants.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，必须招募到合适的人员作为参与者。

sentences.en: As well as the criteria I've mentioned, they have to be comfortable talking about themselves and being watched as they go about their activities.
sentences.zh: 除上述标准外，参与者还必须乐于谈论自身情况，并能自在地接受对其日常活动的观察。

sentences.en: Actually, most researchers say that people open up pretty easily, maybe because they're often in their own home or workplace.
sentences.zh: 实际上，大多数研究人员表示，人们通常很容易敞开心扉，或许是因为他们往往身处自家或工作场所之中。

sentences.en: So what makes this type of research special is that it's not just a matter of sending a questionnaire to the participants, instead the research is usually based on first-hand observation of what they are doing at the time.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种研究的独特之处在于：它并非仅仅向参与者发放问卷，而是通常基于对其当下行为的第一手观察。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that the researcher never talks to the participants.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着研究人员从不与参与者交谈。

sentences.en: However, unlike in traditional research, in this case it's the participant rather than the researchers who decides what direction the interview will follow.
sentences.zh: 然而，与传统研究不同的是，在此类研究中，决定访谈方向的是参与者而非研究人员。

sentences.en: This means that there's less likelihood of the researcher imposing his or her own ideas on the participant.
sentences.zh: 这意味着研究人员将自己的观点强加给参与者的可能性大大降低。

sentences.en: But after they've said goodbye to their participants and got back to their office, the researchers' work isn't finished.
sentences.zh: 但当研究人员与参与者告别并返回办公室后，其工作远未结束。

sentences.en: Most researchers estimate that 70 to 80 per cent of their time is spent not on the collecting of data but on its analysis - looking at photos, listening to ordings and transcribing them, and so on.
sentences.zh: 大多数研究人员估计，他们70%至80%的时间并非用于数据收集，而是用于数据分析——例如查看照片、收听录音并将其转录成文字等。

sentences.en: The researchers may end up with hundreds of pages of notes.
sentences.zh: 研究人员最终可能会得到数百页的笔记。

sentences.en: And to determine what's significant, they don't focus on the sensational things or the unusual things, instead they try to identify a pattern of some sort in all this data, and to discern the meaning behind it.
sentences.zh: 为了确定哪些内容是重要的，他们不会关注耸人听闻或异常的事情，而是试图在所有这些数据中识别出某种模式，并洞察其背后的意义。

sentences.en: This can result in some compelling insights that can in turn feed back to the whole design process.
sentences.zh: 这可能会产生一些引人注目的见解，进而反馈到整个设计过程中。
